findings.summary: __getattr__ does not cache lazy-imported classes in the module namespace, causing the full import to re-execute on every single attribute access
findings.failure_scenario: Any code that accesses azure.ai.evaluation.AIAgentConverter or SKAgentConverter more than once (e.g., in a loop, or from multiple call sites in the same process) re-runs __import__, getattr, and _patch_all.append on every access. The _patch_all list grows without bound on repeated access. Even with dependencies installed, every attribute lookup is a fresh import — classes are never cached in the module globals.

findings.summary: Changing from print+continue to raise ImportError in the except block silently alters import behavior — plain import of the red_team module now requires Pyrit installed
findings.failure_scenario: Previously, import azure.ai.evaluation.red_team would succeed without Pyrit (printing an info message and loading the module without the red-team classes). Now the same import raises ImportError. Code that does import azure.ai.evaluation.red_team and then conditionally checks for available classes (hasattr pattern) will see an ImportError instead of a loaded module.

findings.summary: Tests re-implement _create_lazy_import locally instead of importing the real module — the actual __init__.py lazy-import mechanism is never exercised
findings.failure_scenario: The core bug (__getattr__ not caching) would never be caught by these tests because they test a local copy of the pattern, not the real module. A developer relying on these tests alone would ship the caching defect. The test_no_messages_during_module_import test only asserts that dict assignment does not print, which is vacuously true.

findings.summary: _patch_all.append(class_name) inside lazy_import is dead code — __all__ is already fully computed at module load time before any __getattr__ call can fire
findings.failure_scenario: At module load (line 143), __all__.extend runs against _patch_all which is still empty. When __getattr__ later triggers lazy_import and appends to _patch_all, nobody reads it. The append is harmless but misleading — it suggests the list is still live when it is not.

findings.summary: ImportError re-raise in lazy_import discards the original exception chain by omitting 'from e', losing root-cause context for debugging
findings.failure_scenario: If the underlying import fails for a non-obvious reason (e.g., a transitive dependency version conflict inside _ai_services.py), the original ImportError with its traceback is silently replaced by a generic message. The developer sees only 'Could not import AIAgentConverter. Please install azure-ai-projects' even though azure-ai-projects IS installed but has an internal conflict.
